Scrublet parameters

Source: R/tool-scrublet.R
scrubletParam.Rd

Parameters for GiottoClass::analyzeData() that run Scrublet (Wolock, Lopez and Klein 2019), which detects doublets by simulating them from pairs of observed cells and scoring each cell by the share of simulated doublets among its nearest neighbors. It is meant for single-cell data, not for spots that hold several cells. Scrublet is a Python package: the first run installs it with reticulate (reticulate >= 1.41, no conda). If you use it, please cite the original paper (see References).

Usage

scrubletParam(
  expected_doublet_rate = 0.06,
  min_counts = 1L,
  min_cells = 1L,
  min_gene_variability_pctl = 85,
  n_prin_comps = 30L,
  threshold = NULL,
  seed = 1234L
)

# S4 method for class 'allMatrix,scrubletParam'
analyzeData(x, param, verbose = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

expected_doublet_rate

expected fraction of doublets (0.06 is from the 10x Chromium guide)

min_counts, min_cells

Scrublet's feature filter before its PCA: a feature needs at least min_counts counts in at least min_cells cells

min_gene_variability_pctl

percentile of feature variability above which features are used

n_prin_comps

number of principal components

threshold

NULL (Scrublet sets the doublet score threshold itself) or a score above which cells are called doublets. Scrublet cannot always set one, e.g. on spot data, and then calls no doublets.

seed

integer random state of Scrublet

x

count matrix, features x cells

param

a scrubletParam

verbose

show Scrublet's progress messages

Value

A scrubletParam object.

Details

analyzeData(x, param) returns a data.table with one row per cell: cell_ID, doublet_score and doublet (Scrublet's call, NA when there is no threshold and Scrublet could not set one).

References

Wolock SL, Lopez R, Klein AM. Scrublet: computational identification of cell doublets in single-cell transcriptomic data. Cell Systems 8, 281-291.e9 (2019). doi:10.1016/j.cels.2018.11.005

See also

runScrublet()

Examples

p <- scrubletParam(expected_doublet_rate = 0.08)
p$expected_doublet_rate
